## Abstract

This essay reviews Allcott et al. (2019), “Food Deserts and the Causes of Nutritional Inequality.” It explains the supermarket-entry and household-mover designs, the structural model of grocery demand, and the decomposition of nutritional inequality into supply and demand components. I discuss how the paper arrives at its conclusion that differences in demand explain most of the observed nutrition gap, and how that conclusion informs the comparison between retail-access policies and healthy-food subsidies.
